newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hails Hebron accord, stresses new EU role.
newsitem.headline: France hails Hebron accord, stresses new EU role.

text.p: France hailed a deal between Israel and the PLO on Wednesday extending Palestinian rule to the West Bank town of Hebron and said the long-awaited accord should pave the way to other pacts to bolster peace in the Middle East.

President Jacques Chirac's office released letters of congratulation he sent to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, U.S. President Bill Clinton and the leaders of Jordan and Egypt.

Stressing the courage of Israel's hardline government in reaching its first agreement with the PLO, Chirac said France and the European Union stood ready to contribute to building Arab-Israeli peace in close coordination with the United States.

Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said the EU's special envoy to the region, Miguel-Angel Moratinos, had played a role in brokering the deal and that the EU would for the first time be involved in its implementation.
Moratinos had given Arafat a letter of understandings from the EU complementing U.S. undertakings to the parties.
"France welcomes the agreement between Israelis and Palestinians on the redeployment of the Israeli army in the town of Hebron," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
"This accord has been long awaited; France hopes that it will be implemented as quickly as possible," it said.

"This agreement should be a new departure for all aspects of the peace process," it said, adding: "Other parts of the interim accord on the autonomy of the West Bank and Gaza should now be quickly implemented."

Under the pact, Israel will hand over most of Hebron to Palestinian rule within 10 days. Negotiators initialled the accord on the border between Israel and the Gaza Strip at a late-night summit between Netanyahu and Arafat.

French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure quoted de Charette as telling the cabinet "he was delighted that for the first time, at the request of the protagonists themsleves, the European Union will have a role to play in implementing the accord".
Arafat insisted that the EU be a co-guarantor, along with the United States, of the agreement.
